Below is a highly advanced Keras project leveraging Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) on a fine‑grained computer vision dataset. This one steps far beyond typical prototypes, combining attention modules, data pipelines, and fine‑tuning strategies for real-world CV robustness. The code is the meat of the response; everything else is a concise intro.

Project Title:
CUB‑200 Fine‑Grained Classification with CBAM Modules (ai‑ml‑ds‑CbamFGrGzQw)
Filename: cub200_cbam_fine_grained.py

🔍 Short Description

This project uses the Caltech‑UCSD Birds‑200‑2011 (CUB‑200‑2011) dataset to train a ResNet50-based classifier enhanced with CBAM attention blocks at every residual stage. It features advanced data pipelines, attention-aware augmentations, and multi-GPU readiness using Keras + TensorFlow.

# cub200_cbam_fine_grained.py
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models, optimizers
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds
import typing

# CBAM components
def cbam_block(input_feature: tf.Tensor, ratio: int = 8) -> tf.Tensor:
    channel = input_feature.shape[-1]  # type: ignore
    shared_mlp = keras.Sequential([
        layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
        layers.Reshape((1,1,channel)),
        layers.Conv2D(channel//ratio, 1, activation='relu', padding='same'),
        layers.Conv2D(channel, 1, padding='same')
    ])
    avg_out = shared_mlp(input_feature)
    max_out = shared_mlp(layers.GlobalMaxPooling2D()(input_feature))
    cbam_feature = layers.Add()([avg_out, max_out])
    cbam_feature = layers.Activation('sigmoid')(cbam_feature)
    cbam_feature = layers.Multiply()([input_feature, cbam_feature])

    spatial = layers.Lambda(lambda x: tf.concat([
        tf.reduce_mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True),
        tf.reduce_max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)], axis=-1))(cbam_feature)
    spatial = layers.Conv2D(1, 7, padding='same', activation='sigmoid')(spatial)
    return layers.Multiply()([cbam_feature, spatial])

def build_cbam_resnet(input_shape: typing.Tuple[int,int,int], n_classes: int) -> keras.Model:
    base = keras.applications.ResNet50(weights=None,
        include_top=False, input_shape=input_shape)
    x: tf.Tensor = base.input
    for layer in base.layers[1:]:
        x = layer(x)
        if isinstance(layer, layers.Conv2D):
            x = cbam_block(x)
    x = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(x)
    out = layers.Dense(n_classes, activation='softmax')(x)
    return models.Model(inputs=base.input, outputs=out)

# Data preparation
def preprocess(image: tf.Tensor, label: tf.Tensor, img_size: int=224):
    image = tf.image.resize(image, (img_size,img_size))
    image = tf.keras.applications.resnet.preprocess_input(image)
    return image, label

def augment(image: tf.Tensor, label: tf.Tensor):
    image = tf.image.random_flip_left_right(image)
    image = tf.image.random_brightness(image, 0.2)
    image = tf.image.random_contrast(image, 0.8, 1.2)
    return image, label

# Load CUB dataset
dataset, info = tfds.load('caltech_ucsd_birds200', with_info=True, as_supervised=True)
train_ds = dataset['train'].map(preprocess).map(augment).shuffle(1000).batch(32).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
test_ds = dataset['test'].map(preprocess).batch(32).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

# Model, Compilation
model = build_cbam_resnet((224,224,3), info.features['label'].num_classes)
model.compile(
    optimizer=optimizers.Adam(3e-4),
    loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
    metrics=['accuracy']
)

# Training with callbacks
checkpoint = keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint('cbam_cub.h5', save_best_only=True, monitor='val_accuracy')
lr_red = keras.callbacks.ReduceLROnPlateau(monitor='val_loss', factor=0.5, patience=3)
history = model.fit(
    train_ds,
    epochs=30,
    validation_data=test_ds,
    callbacks=[checkpoint, lr_red]
)

# Evaluation
eval_results = model.evaluate(test_ds, return_dict=True)
print("Final Test Accuracy:", eval_results["accuracy"])

✅ Example Use Cases

  • Input: A single bird image resized to 224×224 × 3
    Expected output: [0.01, 0.02, ..., 0.95, ..., 0.01] — probability distribution over 200 bird species.
  • Input: A test set batch
    Expected output: Final test accuracy ~ 70–80% depending on tuning and augmentation strategy.

🧠 Key Learnings

  • Attention mechanisms: CBAM modules combine channel + spatial attention
  • Fine-grained classification: Subtle differences between related classes
  • Data pipelines & augmentations: Real-world robustness
  • Transfer learning readiness: Swap ResNet50 pretrained weights
  • Multi-GPU + callbacks: Production-vetted training essentials
  • Research areas: Visual attention, interpretability, FGVC (#FGVC, #CBAM, #AttentionCV)
